questions.stem: Hydrochloric acid (0.1 mol/dm³) has a pH of 1, while ethanoic acid (0.1 mol/dm³) has a pH of about 3. Both are at the same concentration. Why are their pH values different?

options.text: Ethanoic acid is more concentrated than hydrochloric acid
HCl fully ionises (strong acid, producing more H+), while ethanoic acid only partially ionises (weak acid, producing fewer H+)
Ethanoic acid is not really an acid
HCl has more hydrogen atoms per molecule

questions.explanation: HCl is a strong acid that fully ionises: HCl -> H+ + Cl- (100% ionisation). Ethanoic acid is a weak acid that only partially ionises: CH3COOH ⇌ CH3COO- + H+ (only about 1% ionises). At the same concentration, the strong acid produces many more H+ ions, giving a lower pH. Weak does NOT mean dilute.

questions.stem: A student says 'concentrated sulfuric acid is a strong acid, and dilute ethanoic acid is a weak acid.' She thinks 'strong' means 'concentrated.' Is she correct?

options.text: Yes, strong and concentrated mean the same thing
No - strong/weak refers to degree of ionisation; concentrated/dilute refers to the amount of acid dissolved per unit volume
Yes, all concentrated acids are strong
No, but only because sulfuric acid is actually a weak acid

questions.explanation: This is a very common misconception. Strong/weak describes how completely the acid ionises (strong = fully ionises; weak = partially ionises). Concentrated/dilute describes how much acid is dissolved in a given volume. You can have a concentrated weak acid (e.g., pure ethanoic acid/vinegar) or a dilute strong acid (e.g., very dilute HCl).

questions.stem: If you react equal concentrations of hydrochloric acid (strong) and ethanoic acid (weak) with identical pieces of magnesium, what difference would you observe?

options.text: Only HCl would react; ethanoic acid would not react at all
HCl would react faster (more vigorous fizzing) because it has a higher concentration of H+ ions
Both would react at exactly the same rate
Ethanoic acid would react faster because it is an organic acid

questions.explanation: Both acids react with magnesium (Mg + 2H+ -> Mg2+ + H2), but HCl reacts faster because it is fully ionised, providing a higher initial concentration of H+ ions. Ethanoic acid reacts more slowly because fewer H+ ions are available at any time (most molecules remain un-ionised). Both would eventually produce the same amount of hydrogen if the same number of moles of acid is used.

questions.stem: The ionisation of ethanoic acid is represented as: CH3COOH ⇌ CH3COO- + H+. The equilibrium symbol (⇌) is used. What does this tell us about weak acid ionisation?

options.text: The ionisation is irreversible
The ionisation is reversible - an equilibrium exists between ionised and un-ionised molecules
The acid fully ionises then reforms
The equilibrium always lies to the right

questions.explanation: The reversible arrow (⇌) shows that weak acid ionisation is a reversible process at equilibrium. Most molecules remain un-ionised (equilibrium lies to the left), with only a small proportion existing as H+ and CH3COO- at any time. For strong acids, a single forward arrow (->) is used because ionisation is complete and irreversible.

questions.stem: A 0.1 mol/dm³ solution of a strong acid has a pH of 1. If the acid is diluted by adding water until the concentration is 0.001 mol/dm³, what is the new pH?

options.text: pH 2
pH 3
pH 4

questions.explanation: For a strong monobasic acid, pH = -log[H+]. At 0.1 mol/dm³, pH = 1. At 0.001 mol/dm³ (10^-3), pH = 3. Each 10-fold dilution increases the pH by 1. Diluting 0.1 to 0.001 is a 100-fold dilution (two factors of 10), so pH increases by 2: from 1 to 3.
